The user wants a block-breaking game (Breakout/Arkanoid). Let me build a rich, polished single-file HTML game with canvas. Key design decisions: - It should open with the game itself — that's the most characteristic thing for a breakout game. An arcade cabinet feel. CRT scanlines, chunky arcade typography, glowing blocks. - Distinctive display face: something arcade-ish. Google Fonts: "Bungee" or "Chakra Petch" or "Press Start 2P" (too cliché pixel but actually appropriate for arcade). Let's pair a strong display face with a readable body face. Maybe "Bungee" display + "Space Grotesk" body? Or "Monoton"? Let's use "Chakra Petch" for body/UI (techy, readable) and "Bungee" for display headings. Actually for an arcade breakout, "Bungee" is chunky and bold. Good contrast. Palette: I want an arcade cabinet glow rather than a flat near-black field with one lone neon accent — that reads cheap for this genre. Let's do a deep midnight-blue/plum cabinet with multiple vivid hues: amber, cyan, magenta, lime for block rows. Background layered: subtle grid, vignette, drifting starfield/particles, CRT scanlines overlay. Game features (rich but purposeful): - Canvas breakout with paddle, ball, brick grid. - Multiple levels with layouts (generated patterns). - Power-ups: expand paddle, multiball, slow ball, laser?, sticky, extra life. Falling capsules. - Particles on brick break, screen shake, ball trail. - Combo multiplier, score popups. - Sound via WebAudio (blips), toggle mute. - HUD: score, lives, level, combo. - Start overlay, level-clear flash, game over screen, pause. - Mouse + keyboard + touch controls. - Micro-interactions on side panel buttons. Layout: an asymmetric layout — left rail with vertical branding/stats, center cabinet screen, right column with power-up legend and level info. A bottom strip with controls. Let me write it carefully. Structure: - Header bar: logo mark, title "BRICKBREAKER" with Bungee, small tagline, mute toggle. - Main: grid with left column (stats: score big number, high score, level, lives as pips), center canvas cabinet, right column (power-up legend, combo meter, mission log / level name). - Below: control hints. Canvas: fixed logical size e.g. 720x520, scaled responsively with CSS, devicePixelRatio handling. Let me code the game. Game constants: - W = 760, H = 540 logical. - Paddle: w 100, h 14, y = H-40. - Ball: r 7, speed base 380 px/s, increases per level. - Bricks: grid cols 12, rows depend on level. brick width = (W - padding*2 - gap*(cols-1))/cols. Brick types: - normal (1 hit) colored by row - tough (2 hits) — armored look - steel (indestructible) - explosive (destroys neighbors) - Each has hue. Power-ups drop chance ~14%: - WIDE (paddle +40%) - MULTI (3 balls) - SLOW (ball speed *0.7) - LIFE (+1) - LASER (paddle shoots, timed) - MAGNET/Sticky? maybe skip; keep LASER, WIDE, MULTI, SLOW, LIFE, and POINTS(+500). Timed effects with a status list shown in HUD. Lives 3. Ball lost -> lose life. Level clear -> next level, +bonus. Levels: define patterns as functions generating brick maps. Let's make 6 patterns and cycle with increasing speed. Effects: particles, screen shake, brick flash, ball trail, glow. Sound: WebAudio simple oscillator blips: paddle hit, brick hit, brick break, powerup, life lost, level clear. Mute toggle. Input: mousemove over canvas, arrow keys / A-D, touch drag. Space/click to launch. Ball sticks to paddle at start ("ready" state). Pause with P or Esc. Let me also add a subtle CRT overlay: scanlines via repeating-linear-gradient, vignette, slight curvature via border-radius + inset shadow. Keep it tasteful. Ambient background: animated gradient mesh? Rather than soft blobs, use a moving grid of faint lines + drifting "brick" glyph shapes + noise. I'll do a CSS animated grid + a few floating pixel squares, plus a canvas-level starfield inside the game background (subtle parallax dots). Let me write the code. grid, motes
